description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated stream closures and an HTTP-level request deadline firing before the final tokens are emitted when using very large max_tokens (150k+) with multi-document priming. Impact: Generation cuts off after 60-120s; downstream UI shows 'Stream closed' while model logs indicate finalization work still in progress. Environment: Dedicated tenant on us-east; runs pinned to rw-long-13b-v2; sustained single-request token budgets of 120k-180k; streaming=on; burst concurrency 2.

Observed behavior: For heavy priming workloads (20+ docs totaling ~100k tokens) the client receives a chunked stream for ~45-90s and then gets an abrupt TCP/HTTP/2 stream close with a 499/408-like symptom on the client (connection closed by server-side deadline). On the serving side we see the inference runtime still performing final KV flush and trailing attention kernel swaps.

Expected behavior: Long-running generations should stream progressively until all tokens are emitted or hit an explicit user timeout. Final flushes should not cause premature connection termination for in-flight streaming sessions.

Customer impact and priority: Production API requests failing for 2 of NarrativeAI's end-user flows (chat export and long-document summarization). They have temporarily disabled long-window exports, impacting revenue. Customer requests urgent mitigation and status updates.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use dedicated tenant credentials for NarrativeAI on us-east
2) Call /v1/generate with model=rw-long-13b-v2, streaming=true, max_tokens=150000, prompt composed of 25 docs totaling ~100k tokens
3) Allow generation to run without client-side timeout for 3+ minutes
4) Observe server-closed stream and incomplete final chunk on the client while the runtime logs show ongoing finalizer activity
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Reproduced with internal dedicated tenant; client shows stream closure while runtime still doing tail work.

Hypothesis A: Per-tenant concurrency shaping interacts poorly with dynamic batching when a single request has an extreme token budget, causing the request to be deprioritized and hit a connection-level deadline upstream (streaming-proxy) even though runtime remains busy.
Hypothesis B: Finalizer thread pool and KV flush path can block on large serial writes; preemptive scheduler actions reduce priority of requests mid-flight leading to 'soft kill' by proxy timeout.

Observations: Queue metrics show repeated priority inversions where small short-lived requests jump ahead of the long generation. The streaming-proxy has a hard idle/read timeout tuned for typical long-polling but not for multi-minute token drains.
Trace links: tracing.trace_id: trc-20260310-xyz -> shows sustained CPU on kernel threads and several 20-40s pauses in user-space writer while kernel swap completes.

Reproduced with streaming=false: when streaming is disabled the HTTP request still completes but with extended finalization time; no early connection close observed (client waits). This suggests the streaming proxy's streaming-specific timeout path is likely involved.
Related configs inspected: tenant.rate_limiter.concurrency=4, streaming_proxy.stream_idle_timeout=60s, finalizer.thread_pool_size=4 (default)
temporary_workarounds: 1) Ask customer to set streaming=false for very large exports (server will wait and return full payload when ready).
2) Reduce max_tokens to <=60k for streaming sessions until permanent fix deployed.
3) For Dedicated tenants: request temporary increase of streaming_proxy.stream_idle_timeout via support config toggle (requires change and quick restart).
resolution: Mitigation in progress: temporarily increased streaming_proxy.stream_idle_timeout to 300s for NarrativeAI tenant to prevent premature stream closures. Scheduled a replay-run for priority scheduler adjustments and plan to increase finalizer thread pool for large-output requests. Engineering has a targeted patch to: 1) respect in-flight long-generation flag in scheduler to avoid priority inversion; 2) extend streaming path keepalive for explicit large-token sessions. Patch PR created and under review.
next_steps: 1) Eng: finish PR to honor long_generation_hint in scheduler and route (resp. https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2891)
2) Eng: increase default finalizer.thread_pool_size for dedicated tiers and add telemetry for long-finalizer latencies
3) Support: coordinate rolling change for NarrativeAI and monitor for 72 hours
4) Postmortem: produce a short incident report and update long-context runbook with guidance for streaming timeouts
